data.reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed both PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, finding a standard VCS package with no malicious behavior: git source points to legitimate upstream GitHub repo, pkgver() only runs git describe, package() uses standard install commands to place files in $pkgdir, no eval/curl/wget/obfuscation. Report 1's inconclusive result was due to an API error (HTTP 400) on the PKGBUILD file, not a security finding. The package follows normal AUR VCS packaging patterns with no injection risks.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in Report 1 (qwen3-235b), which failed with HTTP 400 BadRequestError when auditing the PKGBUILD file. Report 2 successfully completed the audit and found no issues. This is not a genuine security disagreement but an infrastructure failure.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to complete PKGBUILD audit due to API error (HTTP 400), leaving that file inconclusive
learnings: API errors should be clearly distinguished from security findings in verdict aggregation - a tool failure is not evidence of risk
When one report fails due to infrastructure error and another completes successfully with thorough analysis, the successful report should carry decisive weight

Standard VCS packaging patterns (git+https source, sha256sums=SKIP, pkgver using git describe) should be recognized as safe by default unless there's evidence of executing fetched content or fetching from unrelated hosts
